description: Figure 3.2 is a line plot titled “Finetuning for different r, Gazeta” that illustrates how the ROUGE-1 score changes with different values of the parameter \(r\) (shown as \(\log r\)) for two model families (T5 and MBart) using two adapter methods (LoRA and AdaLoRA). The x-axis is labeled “log r,” uses a linear scale, and shows integer tick marks from 0 to 9 at a regular interval of 1. The y-axis is labeled “ROUGE-1,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from 0 up to about 35 with evenly spaced tick marks (gridlines suggest 5-point increments). Four solid lines with circular markers are shown: the red line (T5 + LoRA) stays nearly flat around the mid‑20s, starting near 23 at \(\log r=0\) and remaining around 24–24.5 through \(\log r=9\); the green line (MBart + LoRA) increases steadily from about 23 at \(\log r=0\) to about 30 by \(\log r=9\), with intermediate values around 25 at \(\log r=2\), ~27 at \(\log r=4\), and ~29–30 from \(\log r=5\) onward; the purple line (T5 + AdaLoRA) begins near 5 at \(\log r=0\), rises to about 8 at \(\log r=1\), drops to about 2–3 at \(\log r=2\), then climbs sharply to about 19 at \(\log r=4\) and levels in the low‑to‑mid 20s from \(\log r=5\) to 9 (around ~22.5–24, ending near ~23–24); the orange line (MBart + AdaLoRA) starts near 5 at \(\log r=0\), increases through roughly 9 (\(\log r=1\)), ~13 (\(\log r=2\)), and ~19 (\(\log r=3\)), then jumps to about 32 at \(\log r=4\) and stays near 33–34 from \(\log r=5\) through \(\log r=9\).
